mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 falling for two consecutive quarters) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 98 for two consecutive months) signals supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate revenue and increases input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO < 98 for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between CPIAUCSL rising above 3% and FEDFUNDS remaining below 4% for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure without a tight monetary response, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS < 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS < 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 6-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3%).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 6-mo SMA and HOUST < 6-mo SMA for 2 consecutive months, and FEDFUNDS >= 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 6-month moving averages for two months and FEDFUNDS >= 3%.
